name: Red House Painters
label: 4AD
lede: Mark Kozelek's band got signed off a 90-minute demo tape, made four long, slow records for 4AD, then left the label and got caught in Island's merger. Its final album sat on a shelf for three years before Kozelek bought it back.

eras.title: From Atlanta to the Mission, on a demo budget
eras.text: Mark Kozelek, from Massillon, Ohio, met drummer Anthony Koutsos in Atlanta after his teenage band God Forbid split. Atlanta labels passed, so they moved west and filled out the band in San Francisco.

years.src: Wikipedia: Red House Painters · Wikipedia: Mark Kozelek
years.h: Kozelek and Koutsos start the band in Atlanta
years.p: They play shows and record, but can't get a label interested in Atlanta.

years.h: San Francisco adds a bassist and a second guitar
years.p: Bassist [[Jerry Vessel|affc95a1-c207-431d-af46-995afad2184a]] and guitarist Gorden Mack join. The band plays around San Francisco and keeps recording demos through 1992.

eras.title: Long songs for 4AD
eras.text: A tape that ran an hour and a half got them a deal with a British label, which released the demos nearly as they were. Over three years the band put out four albums, with songs that often ran past seven minutes.

q: Never before or since had I received a demo that was 90 minutes long!
years.h: Mark Eitzel passes on a 90-minute demo
years.p: [[American Music Club|5837d14e-4d18-49cf-a759-e5818714bce4]]'s Mark Eitzel gives the tape to journalist Martin Aston, who gets it to 4AD's [[Ivo Watts-Russell|cf86cec1-1baf-4d8a-ba1e-01568332585a]]. Watts-Russell listens to all of it and calls Kozelek.

years.src: Wikipedia: Down Colorful Hill · NME: Painter Your Wagon
yt: Grace Cathedral Park, live in London, 1992
years.h: Down Colorful Hill is the demo, slightly remixed
years.p: Six songs from the 1989–91 tapes; the title track runs 10:51. 4AD had done the same with debuts by [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]] and [[Lush|697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1]].
years.xp:
Kozelek later said he regretted the heavy reverb and echo in the mix. The cover is a photograph called Bed by Simon Larbalestier. The Philadelphia Inquirer compared the record to a chilly, fogbound English morning.

NME met him that November, with a double album already on the way. "I don't drink, I don't use drugs, I live a pretty solitary life," Kozelek told John Mulvey; writing was how he reacted to things.

years.p: The first of two self-titled albums is known by its cover, a sepia photo of Coney Island's demolished Thunderbolt roller coaster. It reaches No. 63 in the UK.
years.xp: Kozelek produced it in a studio on Divisadero Street in San Francisco between summer 1992 and spring 1993. Grace Cathedral Park opens it and Mistress was the single. Spin's James Greer wrote that it rewards patient listening.

years.cap: Music-paper advert for the band's 1993 tour
years.h: The leftovers come out five months later, with a Star-Spangled Banner
years.p: The second self-titled album, known as Bridge, has eight songs from the same sessions, including a cover of Paul Simon's I Am a Rock.

years.src: Wikipedia: Red House Painters · Wikipedia: Red House Painters (Bridge)
years.h: Two versions of a Kiss song on the Shock Me EP
years.p: Kozelek covers [[Kiss|e1f1e33e-2e4c-4d43-b91b-7064068d3283]]'s Shock Me, written by Ace Frehley, once electric and once acoustic.

yt: Live at the Alligator Lounge, Santa Monica, 1995
years.h: Ocean Beach ends with a 13-minute track hiding a sequel
years.p: Recorded at Coast Recorders in San Francisco. Drop closes it, with a hidden second part of Brockwell Park inside.
years.xp: The Summer Dress video was shot on 16mm by Matt Amato, on a vintage streetcar and in San Francisco's Victoria Theater. Entertainment Weekly gave the album an A, and Pitchfork ranked it No. 58 of the 1990s in 1999.

years.src: Wikipedia: Red House Painters · Wikipedia: Ocean Beach
yt: Live on KFOG, San Francisco, Dec 3, 1995
years.p: Phil Carney replaces the founding guitarist.

eras.title: Dropped, merged, shelved
eras.text: 4AD wouldn't put out the next record, and the label that would was soon swallowed by the late-'90s mergers. The band was coming apart while its last album waited.

years.src: Wikipedia: Songs for a Blue Guitar · Uncut: Mark Kozelek interviewed
years.h: 4AD won't release Songs for a Blue Guitar
years.p: Watts-Russell's later verdict on letting the band go. Kozelek had offered to put it out as a solo record and was turned down.
years.xp:
Stories differ on why. One says Watts-Russell objected to the long guitar solos; Wikipedia calls strained relations between Kozelek and 4AD's Warner-controlled American office more likely.

Uncut's 2015 buyer's guide still tells the guitar-solo version, with an "allegedly."

years.src: Wikipedia: Songs for a Blue Guitar · Wikipedia: Red House Painters · Uncut: Mark Kozelek interviewed
years.h: Songs for a Blue Guitar becomes the band's best US seller
years.p: Out on Supreme Recordings, the John Hughes-owned label distributed by Island. It's loud and electric, with covers of Wings, Yes and [[The Cars|092b603f-eb4c-4958-b10e-02420de5885b]].
years.xp:
No other band member is in the liner notes, which makes it close to a Kozelek solo album, though all four play in the All Mixed Up video. The covers are Silly Love Songs, Long Distance Runaround and All Mixed Up. Pitchfork gave it 9.0.

Hughes came with conversation. Kozelek once spent seven hours on the phone with him trying to borrow money: "I just wanted to get $15,000. Listening to him talk for seven hours was the price I had to pay."

years.src: Wikipedia: Old Ramon · Wikipedia: Mark Kozelek
years.h: Island's merger strands a finished Old Ramon
years.p: Recorded from fall 1997 to spring 1998, the album stalls in the Island merger. Kozelek ends up buying it back from Island.
The old label's best-of arrives while the new album is still stuck.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mark Kozelek · Wikipedia: Red House Painters
years.h: Kozelek plays Stillwater's bassist in Almost Famous
years.p: He's Larry Fellows in Cameron Crowe's film. The same year his Rock 'n' Roll Singer EP turns Bon Scott-era AC/DC songs into acoustic folk.
years.xp: A full album of AC/DC covers, What's Next to the Moon, followed in 2001 on Badman Recordings, and Crowe gave him a part in Vanilla Sky the same year.

years.cap: Phil Carney, Mark Kozelek, Jerry Vessel and Anthony Koutsos, 2001
years.h: Sub Pop releases Old Ramon, three years late
years.p: It opens with a song for Kozelek's cat and became known as a lost record during its time on the shelf. It is the band's last album.
years.xp: Metacritic averaged 84 and Alternative Press gave it five out of five. Craig Ross and Michael Urbano are among the extra players.

eras.title: Same songwriter, new name
eras.text: Kozelek kept working with Koutsos under a new name, and said plainly what it was. The 4AD records came back on vinyl in 2015.

years.cap: Kozelek with Sun Kil Moon in Houston
years.h: Kozelek and Koutsos come back as Sun Kil Moon
years.p: [[Sun Kil Moon|ef2c6449-d02b-415b-ad8c-c14c08266552]]'s Ghosts of the Great Highway adds Geoff Stanfield and Tim Mooney. Duk Koo Kim and other songs began as Red House Painters material.
years.xp:
Kozelek told the A.V. Club in 2005 that Sun Kil Moon was essentially a continuation of Red House Painters, renamed to catch the ear of critics who'd stopped paying attention to the old band.

Phil Carney still sometimes plays second guitar with Kozelek on tour. Koutsos became a real estate agent in San Francisco.

years.src: Wikipedia: Red House Painters · Pitchfork: Red House Painters box set review · Uncut: Mark Kozelek interviewed
years.h: The 4AD years on six LPs for Record Store Day
years.p: A Red House Painters vinyl box set is a Record Store Day exclusive.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Brandon Stosuy made the four 4AD albums Best New Reissue in May 2015. Before the internet, he wrote, you knew only what the jewel box told you, and "that mystery somehow still remains."

Kozelek, the same year, told Uncut he no longer played Red House Painters songs live.
